findings.observed: The variable guide says ?= assigns an undefined or empty variable. Both explicit-empty controls retain the empty value; only the genuinely undefined setting receives its default.

A command-line CFLAGS override prevents the ordinary Makefile append from adding project include paths. Original compilation fails at the required header; separate project options preserve successful compilation.

Original target-specific output assignments do not change already-expanded prerequisites. Debug then release both execute debug code from build/shared. The explicit separate-path prototype yields debug and release behavior respectively.

The recommended semicolon sequence continues after cd fails, runs a parent-directory target and returns zero. The checked directory change rejects the missing directory and reaches the intended child when it exists.
Original equal-stem C/C++ mappings lose the C++ translation unit and fail at link. Extension-preserving object paths build both language units and the executable prints 42.

Original uninstall appends build/demo below the installed binary directory and leaves its installed demo behind despite exit zero. Matching the installed basename removes it and preserves an unrelated staged file.

qualified_rule_distinction: Clearing suffixes removes the observed implicit C-object link but leaves RCS checkout patterns in the rule database; --no-builtin-rules removes those patterns while the explicit app rule still works. No checkout command was executed.

rejected_hypothesis.hypothesis: An implicit C-object link would remain after clearing suffix rules.
rejected_hypothesis.observed: Rejected by the v2 run and preserved as an expected negative observation in v3. No hidden C-link finding is claimed.
